description.p: nailong is a lightweight Minecraft: Java Edition launcher written in Rust. Choose a Minecraft version and Fabric, NeoForge, Forge or vanilla, watch the install progress, and launch the game with an offline account. Incomplete downloads are detected and can be repaired.
It ships as a single native executable with no bundled runtime and keeps the launcher itself small.

CurseForge credentials are now built in and lightly obfuscated; the user-facing API key setting and local settings file were removed. Maintainers can still override the key with an environment variable.

Official builds include a project CurseForge API key so regular users can import CurseForge packs without configuring one. Runtime environment variables and user settings still take precedence; the embedded key is extractable and treated as a shared default quota.
Install cancellation: downloads, extraction and loader processors now respond to a cancel button; completed parts are kept for the next repair.

CurseForge compliance fixes: respect files whose authors disabled third-party distribution, use the official download page instead of synthesizing CDN URLs, space out metadata requests, and support an optional build-time default key.

The settings page can store a CurseForge API key for official file metadata, size and SHA1 verification. The key is masked, written to the data directory with owner-only permissions on Unix, and never logged.
Modpack imports now cover Modrinth, CurseForge, Prism/MultiMC, MCBBS, HMCL and ATLauncher, with optional CurseForge API hashes.
Modpack imports: Modrinth .mrpack, CurseForge manifest zip and Prism/MultiMC exports, with format detection and loader installation.
Downloader upgrades: four-way range download for large single files, resumable segment parts, cross-source fallback, and a 180-second transfer timeout.
Content-addressed patched-client reuse: scan existing launcher roots, verify, and hardlink instead of downloading the patch or running processors.
Parallel install pipeline: assets, client/libraries, loader patch and processors now run concurrently where dependencies allow.
Size-optimized release (about 7.6 MB), a machine-wide patch cache, and the version management from 0.4.3.

Loader base versions are hidden from the main picker, with a management page for deleting versions and instances. Reinstalling an intact loader is now instant, and the 3 MB core data is fetched in parallel.
Forge and NeoForge installs now fetch only the core installer data (about 3 MB) instead of the full 7–9 MB package; mirrors without range support fall back safely.
Fabric, NeoForge, Forge and vanilla installs, with version pickers, progress and repair.
